prompt:
Produce exactly one concise, information‑dense caption (one grammatical sentence) describing only visibly present facts. Output exactly one sentence and nothing else.

Follow this ordered checklist and include each item only if clearly visible; omit unverifiable items. Use digits for counts. Do not infer, hedge, or use metaphors (no "appears/likely/seems"). Keep the sentence compact (prefer ≤30 words) and comma‑separate short phrases.

Order and rules:
1) Start with numeral(s) (digit) + subject noun(s) + precise spatial anchor for each counted subject (left/center/right and foreground/midground/background). If subject is partly out of frame, state "partially cropped at [edge]".
2) Immediately after, include a single visible action if present, and specify the body/vehicle part or object involved (e.g., "right hand on handlebar", "left foot stepping", "rear wheel off ground"). If no clear action is visible, use the token "no-action-visible" or omit the action.
3) Add 1–3 high‑signal descriptor(s) (prefer material/texture, readable text, reflection/wetness, or a distinctive accessory). If legible text appears, transcribe it exactly and localize it (e.g., "'NO PARKING' stenciled on roll-up door at background right"). Cap descriptors to 1–3 short facts (color + material/unique accessory preferred).
4) Choose exactly one viewpoint token if discernible: close-up | medium | wide | high-angle | low-angle.
5) Choose exactly one lighting token if visible: backlit | front-lit | rim-lit | long-shadow-left | long-shadow-right.
6) Choose exactly one short background landmark/texture phrase if visible (single noun phrase, e.g., "wet pavement with ripples", "yellow picnic table", "roll-up door", "plywood roof").
7) For people interacting with structures, require pose + placement wording (e.g., "clinging to top edge near peak, legs dangling"). For visible building construction, include clear cues when present (exposed studs, plywood, insulation).
8) No hedging, no inferred attributes (age, emotion, relationships) beyond visible appearance (hair color, clothing, accessories). Use compact, active phrasing and concrete nouns.

Ordering to follow in the sentence: numeral(s) + subject(s)/location, action+part (if any), discriminative descriptor(s) (max 3), viewpoint token, lighting token, background token.

Examples:
Positive (desired): "3 children center foreground, right child stepping in ankle‑deep puddle; blue raincoat with yellow drawstrings and sunglasses on center child's forehead; medium; backlit; beige van behind."
Negative (avoid): "Several kids standing in water, some wearing colorful clothes, a vague busy background with unclear objects and lighting."
